questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?
questions.correctAnswerText: When defects have been fixed
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only after defects have been repaired or confirmed as not needing repair.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during a trip, not just at the beginning and end. Watch the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to notice early warning signs.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early, well before you turn or change lanes
Keep signaling until the turn is complete
Don't signal if no one is nearby

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't signal if no one is nearby
questions.explanation: Always signal before turns and lane changes, whether or not other vehicles are near. Signal early and keep signaling throughout the move.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not pass slower vehicles
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Turn gently and avoid passing other vehicles unless absolutely necessary.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It takes your mind and hands away from driving
A message may upset the driver
People become too focused on their phones

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your mind and hands away from driving
questions.explanation: Texting is dangerous because it distracts your mind from the road and requires you to remove at least one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: One way to avoid aggressive driving is to:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan realistic travel times
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays. This prevents frustration that can lead to aggressive driving. Also drive at safe speeds, keep a safe distance, avoid gestures, and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: To drive doubles and triples smoothly and prevent rollover, a driver should:

options.text: Drive on the shoulder when possible
Drive faster than the speed limit
Look far ahead to react to problems early

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead to react to problems early
questions.explanation: Watch far ahead of your vehicle. This lets you slow down or change lanes gradually when you see hazards coming.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Store compressed air for the brakes
Should be drained after every trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Store compressed air for the brakes
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air used by the air brake system. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: When you need to stop in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop
Keep your vehicle in a straight line

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle in a straight line
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight while still allowing you to turn if needed. Use controlled braking or stab braking.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people getting out
questions.explanation: Be careful passing parked vehicles. A person may step out suddenly or open a door without looking. Parked drivers may also start moving without seeing you.

questions.question: Using the brakes creates heat. If too much heat is produced, what happens?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: Brakes are designed to handle heat, but excessive heat can cause brake fade. This means the brakes lose their ability to slow the vehicle. Drivers should also use engine braking to help slow down and prevent brakes from overheating.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a possible cause of a vehicle fire?
questions.correctAnswerText: Rolling down the window
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can be caused by spilled fuel, under-inflated tires, electrical short circuits, smoking near fuel, loose fuel connections, and flammable cargo that is not sealed or ventilated properly. Rolling down the window does not cause fires.

questions.question: When is a tank endorsement required?

options.text: When transporting both liquids and gases.
It is optional when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: When transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to operate a tank vehicle that carries either liquids or gases.

questions.question: What does a speed limit posted on a curve mean for double or triple trailers?

options.text: It is safe to drive at that speed in a double or triple.
It is the minimum speed for a double or triple.
It could be too fast for a double or triple.
You should drive faster in a double or triple.

questions.correctAnswerText: It could be too fast for a double or triple.
questions.explanation: A posted speed on a curve may be safe for a straight truck or single trailer. However, it could be too fast for a double or triple trailer rig.

questions.question: What should the trailer hand valve be used for?

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: To test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while driving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always do a routine vehicle inspection before driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do before backing a truck?

options.text: Walk around the area to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the area to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to check the path and look for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so you cannot rely on them alone. Use a helper whenever possible.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: In a different order each time.
In the same order every time.
They are not needed if the vehicle seems fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Always do vehicle inspections in the same order. This helps you learn the steps and makes sure you do not forget to check anything.

questions.question: When coupling a triple trailer rig, which trailer should be coupled first?

options.text: The trailer immediately behind the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer immediately behind the cab.
questions.explanation: Couple the trailer behind the cab first. Then connect the second and third converter dollies and trailers in order.

questions.question: Which behavior shows you might be an aggressive driver?

options.text: You expect delays on your drive.
You slow down and keep a safe following distance.
You make hand gestures that anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You make hand gestures that anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, keeping a safe following distance, and not making hand gestures at other drivers.
